headline.abstract_claim_old: At every resolution ... no zone ever runs out of bicycles
headline.dry_cells_172_condition: hourly, unscaled cell path; the stated 5-minute 1/p-scaled path gives 2,306

coarse.interpretation: 300 m: 0 of 5,263 cells have any neighbour (nearest centre 426 m), so the walk branch never fires. 450 m: 4,885 cells have 1-2 neighbours, all east-west; 378 edge cells have none. 600 m: 5,091 cells have neighbours; east-west 426 m and north-south 556 m are reachable, diagonal 700 m is not. R=0.70 is identical to R=0.60 because the diagonal distance is slightly above 0.700 km. The 172 cells with no neighbour at R=600 are numerically coincidental with the paper's 172 dry cells and are unrelated.
coarse.anisotropy: A circular radius on a rectangular lattice is an artifact: at 450 m the reachable graph is a one-dimensional east-west chain, not a disc.

fine.interpretation: At 0.0025 deg the spacings are 213 m east-west, 278 m north-south and 350 m diagonal. A 300 m radius now reaches 1-4 real neighbours (mean 2.93), so the 300 m experiment finally exercises walking; 450 m reaches mean 7.0 and 600 m mean 13.4. Resolution and radius are therefore not separable in the coarse-grid comparison.

simulator_defect.old_behaviour: I[j] -= 1 removed a bicycle from the donor cell, but the in-flight arrival pool was fed only from `take` (bicycles taken at the departure cell). Every walked trip deleted one bicycle.
simulator_defect.fix: borrow[c] counts walked trips; the zone loop schedules take[idx].sum() + borrow[idx].sum() arrivals, so a borrowed ride re-enters the fleet through the same one-step in-flight pool. The destination kernel remains the demand cell's zone.
simulator_defect.baseline_effect: At R=300 m no neighbour is reachable, borrowed=0, so the published 13.4% curve is bit-identical; the fix changes only R>=426 m runs.
simulator_defect.consequence: Before the fix, unmet rose with radius (R=450 14.90%, R=600 20.52% at 343,638) because bicycles were being deleted; those numbers are invalid.

simulation_results.reading: At the paper's 343,638 calibration the five-seed mean is 13.41% at R=300 (13.4257% for seeds 0-2, exactly the stored curve), 5.84% at R=450 and 2.35% at R=600. At the closed-fleet centre 495,540 the same radii give 9.13%, 3.51% and 1.28%. The main coarse-grid specification asked for by the task (R=450, alpha=1) is therefore 5.84% at 343,638 and 3.51% at 495,540.

dry_cells.paper_claim: some 172 of 5,263 cells do run dry
dry_cells.finding: 172 is reproduced exactly by an HOURLY, UNSCALED deterministic cell path I_c(t)=I0c+cumsum(arrivals-departures). The 5-minute 1/p-scaled path described in the paper gives 2,306; hourly scaled gives 2,251; 5-minute unscaled gives 175. No LP rerun was done: q2_plan.npz and q2_solution.npz are zone-level (50 zones), so they cannot yield a count over 5,263 cells. Robustness: all 12 hourly phase offsets give 169-174 dry cells (172 at three of them), and a one-step arrival lag also gives 172; the match is not a single lucky timestamp.

hourly_unscaled.note: all dry cells are low-stock cells; the path is hourly and unscaled, so only small I0 cells cross zero

stochastic_343638.model: CellSim at FLEET=343,638, 5-min steps; 'dry' = end-of-step inventory < 1 at least once
stochastic_343638.note: separate model; never substituted for the fluid count

dry_cells.side_by_side_rule: The fluid count and the stochastic count are different models and are never substituted for one another. The stochastic count is cells whose end-of-step inventory is below one bicycle at least once; it rises from 2,463 at R=300 to 2,778 at R=450 even though unserved departures fall from 13.41% to 5.84%, because walking moves emptiness between cells.

last_trip_end.note: main I0 gives each no-evidence cell its zone's median positive last-trip-end count; the zero-evidence variant leaves them at 0

fine_grid.support_verdict: supported, with reduced coverage. Cell dimensions 213 x 278 m are 3.64x the constant GPS error (58.5 m lon, 76.4 m lat), and the median retained cell has 257 trips over 10 days (p10 104). But 85.9% of box-filtered trips map to retained fine cells versus 95.6% at 0.005 deg, and typical-day departures are 90.2% of the coarse total, so the fine-grid level is not directly comparable to the coarse level without the demand-matched row.

i0_no_evidence.note: main I0 gives each no-evidence cell its zone's median positive last-trip-end count; the zero-evidence variant leaves them at 0

abstract_24_27.english: The 50-zone inventory never goes negative: the smallest zone holds 1,986 bicycles at midnight and the worst cumulative excursion is -349. At neighbourhood scale the shortage is local, not systemic. On the 0.005-degree grid a 300 m walk reaches no neighbouring cell, so the earlier 13.4% is a no-walking bound; with a 450 m walk unmet demand is 5.8% at the paper's 343,638-bicycle calibration and 3.5% at the closed-fleet estimate of 495,540. A 0.0025-degree grid covering 86% of trips gives 2.1% at 495,540. The system has enough bicycles; it does not have them everywhere.

sec9_106_108.english: The consequence is a wide range in the simulated service level at cell resolution. In the zone-level inventory path of Section Q2 no zone goes negative. On the 0.005-degree grid, a 300 m radius reaches no neighbouring cell centre (the nearest is 426 m), so 13.4% is the no-walking bound. With a 450 m radius, unmet demand is 5.8% at 343,638 bicycles and 3.5% at the closed-fleet estimate of 495,540; 600 m gives 2.3% and 1.3%. On a 0.0025-degree grid, which covers 86% of trips, 450 m gives 2.1%.

replacement_text.note: The final clause of the abstract ('The system has enough bicycles; it does not have them everywhere') is a suggested framing, not a decision; the reviewer may keep the facts and change the conclusion. The sentence immediately above the abstract replacement still carries the T001-R2 fleet rewrite and is not changed here.

notes: The 172 dry-cell number is not an LP result. The Q2 LP files are zone-level (50 zones); the only reconstruction that gives 172 is an hourly, unscaled cell path. The paper says the path is 1/p-scaled; the 5-minute scaled path gives 2,306. T012 must decide which statement to keep.

At 0.005 deg, R=450 reaches only east-west neighbours (426 m) and R=600 adds north-south (556 m); diagonal neighbours (700 m) are not reachable until R>0.700. This anisotropy is an artifact of a circular radius on a rectangular lattice, not a walking model.

A 0.0025 deg cell is 213 x 278 m, 3.64x the constant GPS error; it is above the coordinate resolution but 14.1% of box-filtered trips fall in sub-threshold fine cells, so the fine-grid level is supported with reduced coverage, not as a full-city estimate.

The fine-grid fleet is fixed at 495,540 while its demand base is 90.2% of the coarse base; the demand-matched row (446,959 bicycles) is the like-for-like comparison and gives 2.39% rather than 2.07% at R=450, alpha=1. After the simulator's 1/0.128 scaling the coarse day has 2.14M departures and the fine day 1.93M; all quoted unmet figures are ratios on their own demand base.

On the fine grid the original 300 m radius is physically active and gives 4.77% at 495,540; the coarse 300 m run is no-walking. If the paper keeps the 300 m label, the fine-grid number is the defensible one; the coarse R=450 number is the task's main specification.

A walked trip is dispatched with the demand cell's zone destination kernel, not the donor cell's; adjacent cells can cross a KMeans zone boundary, so this is an approximation. The donor choice is 'the reachable cell with the most bicycles'; nearest-first and random donor rules are untested.
No-evidence I0 cells: 25 of 11,269 (0.22%), carrying 0.043% of typical departures; giving them the zone-median default instead of zero changes the R=450 result by less than 0.02 percentage points.

Untested branches: non-circular walking areas; real pedestrian networks and barriers; walking willingness that depends on distance, weather or bike availability; competition between walkers; time-varying radius; the diagonal at exactly 0.70 km; the alpha=0.2 curve under walking; Q2 LP rerun (T007) and Q4 siting rerun (T009) are out of scope.
The seed spread is Monte Carlo only (0.03-0.24 percentage points); model uncertainty from p, fleet and I0 is larger and is not included in the quoted standard deviations.
The replacement texts are suggestions only; paper/ is byte-identical to the T001 start fingerprint and no conclusion is decided here.
